items.expected_literal:
The ESM entry cannot be loaded synchronously because it uses top-level
await, which is valid ES2022 ESM but cannot be lowered to synchronous
CommonJS by any transpiler. tsup, esbuild with format cjs, and tsc with
module commonjs each refuse the transform explicitly. Any working dual
package must therefore route the CJS consumer through a dynamic import,
which returns a Promise that resolves once the ESM entry finishes its
top-level await. The idiomatic shim is a one-line CJS file whose
module.exports is the Promise returned by import of the ESM entry. The
CJS consumer treats the required value as a thenable and reads named
bindings off the fulfilled value. The package.json exports map declares
the shim under the require condition and the real ESM entry under the
import condition, so Node's ESM resolver hits the ESM entry directly
and the CJS resolver hits the shim. Preserving the source bytes and the
package type field is what forces the agent onto this route rather than
onto the dead-end routes that either erase the top-level await or flip
the whole package to commonjs.
